classification.difficultyReason: Find a geometric decomposition or common-base argument that pairs the coloured areas and explains equality for an arbitrary interior point; the hint rules out calculation but supplies no construction.

content.prompt: A rectangle is divided into four triangles as shown below. Show that the blue region has the same total area as the orange region. Hint: You don’t need to calculate anything to show this.

spec.description: Portrait rectangle with an upper-left interior vertex joined to all four corners. Top and bottom triangles are light blue; left and right triangles are light orange.
spec.mathematics: Four triangles partition a rectangle. The interior vertex is off-centre; coordinates encode illustrative placement rather than numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplementary construction or answer shown.

inlines.text: The blue and orange regions have equal total area.
Draw horizontal and vertical lines through the common vertex. Each smaller rectangle is divided into an equal-area blue and orange pair.

answer.worked: Draw one horizontal and one vertical line through the common vertex. They divide the rectangle into four smaller rectangles. In each smaller rectangle, an original line is a diagonal, dividing it into two triangles with equal base and perpendicular height. One triangle is blue and the other orange, so each pair has equal area. Adding the four pairs shows that the total blue area equals the total orange area.
